text: You're at the supermarket, eyeing a big sale. Your favorite cereal, deeply discounted! A rush of excitement. You're ready to load up and save big.
You grab four boxes, maybe five. Then, that small sign: "Limit 3 per customer." That familiar deflating feeling. Why can't you just buy more?
You might think it's about fairness, stopping hoarders, or ensuring everyone gets some. Or pushing you to buy other full-price items. But these aren't the main reasons.
The real system is clever. Businesses use limits to sort customers. If you need a few, you're a bargain hunter. If you need many, you'll pay full price.
This limit isn't just inventory; it's subtle price discrimination. They discount for one group, ensuring another pays the standard rate. You're categorized.
So next time you see that "limit 3" sign, you won't just see a restriction. You'll understand the invisible system, guiding your choices and managing profits.
